g4ela-26-1-morphology: Some word parts tell you when and where. Pre means before. Re means again, or back. Trans means across. Inter means between. Find the part at the front, ask what it adds to the word, and set one more treasure back in its place.
g4ela-26-2-grammar: And and or are small words with big jobs. And says both things are true. Or says choose one. The bread and the cheese means you get both. The bread or the cheese means you get one. When you see or, ask: what is the choice?
g4ela-26-3-spelling: Long words look scary until you take them apart. Peel off the beginning and the ending first. What’s left is usually a word you already know. Unhappy: take off un, and there’s happy. Then the syllables almost split themselves.
g4ela-26-4-grammar: Editing day. Read each sentence that uses and or or out loud. Ask if it’s doing the right job. And adds. Or offers a choice. And if a sentence has and, and, and, and, it’s time to cut a few and let one idea lead.
